name: Loose Anagen Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Loose Anagen Hair Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Positive hair pull test with painless extraction of anagen hairs
Microscopic examination showing anagen hairs with ruffled cuticles and absent inner root sheath
Sparse, thin, and slow-growing hair with easily pluckable hairs
Positive family history of similar hair abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: positive hair pull test, characteristic microscopic hair findings, and clinical hair appearance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by microscopic hair analysis.

genetic: Mutations in K6HF gene (keratin 6 hair follicle-specific) reported in some familial cases
other: Microscopic hair examination showing anagen hairs with absent inner root sheath and ruffled cuticle
Positive hair pull test with painless extraction of anagen hairs

distinguishingFeatures: Increased telogen hairs rather than anagen hairs on hair pull test
Hair shedding often triggered by systemic stress or illness
Patchy hair loss with exclamation mark hairs
Presence of scalp inflammation or nail changes
Positive autoimmune markers in some cases
Hair shaft fragility with nodes and breakage
Microscopic evidence of hair shaft fractures
No abnormality in hair root sheath

redFlags: Rapid progression of hair loss with scalp inflammation
Systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss accompanying hair loss
references: Messenger AG, et al. Loose Anagen Hair Syndrome. Dermatol Clin. 2013;31(1):41-48.
Hordinsky MK. Loose Anagen Hair Syndrome: Clinical and Genetic Features. Dermatol Ther. 2006;19(3):146-150.
